posts.why: The list itself is the joke and the diagnosis.

tiktok.hook: This business sells nine things and leads with none of them.
beats: All in one menu, none first
tiktok.vo: This business sells nine things: catering, laundry, errands, printing, event decor, and four more, all listed at the same size on the same screen. A stranger cannot pick one, so they pick nothing. The list is not the problem, the flatness is, because everything at the same volume is silence.
tiktok.cap: Nine services, all the same size. A stranger cannot pick one, so they pick nothing.
tiktok.body: Nine services, all listed at the same size on the same screen. A stranger cannot pick one, so they pick nothing. The list is not the problem — the flatness is. Everything at the same volume is silence.

instagram.cap:
Nine services at identical size, on one screen, in one voice. Nobody chooses from a list that refuses to choose. One of them has to be louder than the other eight.

Everything at the same volume is silence.

facebook.body:
A business I looked at sells nine things: catering, laundry, errands, printing, event decor and four more — all at the same size, on the same screen.

A stranger cannot pick one, so they pick nothing.

The list is not the problem. The flatness is. Everything at the same volume is silence.

What is the one thing you would want a stranger to remember?

posts.why: A line people repeat after hearing it once.

tiktok.hook: "We do everything" means "we are not first at anything".
tiktok.vo: We do everything means we are not first at anything, and customers do not search for everything. They search for a thing, on a day, near them, at a price. Being one of nine is being none of the nine, and the person who is first at one of them gets the call.
tiktok.cap: Nobody searches for "everything". They search for one thing on one day.
tiktok.body: We do everything means we are not first at anything. Nobody searches for everything — they search for a thing, on a day, near them, at a price. Being one of nine is being none of the nine.

instagram.cap:
Every extra service you lead with divides the attention you needed for one. Being first at one thing beats being tenth at nine, and it is cheaper to advertise.

One of nine is none of the nine.

facebook.body:
'We do everything' means 'we are not first at anything'.

Nobody searches for everything. They search for a thing, on a day, near them, at a price.

Being one of nine is being none of the nine — and the person who is first at one of them gets the call.

Which one are you actually first at?

posts.topic: Lead with one offer for thirty days
posts.why: A time-boxed experiment, which is easy to agree to.

tiktok.hook: Lead with one offer for thirty days, then add the second.
tiktok.vo: Lead with one offer for thirty days. Same offer, every post, different angle. Not because the others are bad, but because thirty days is the shortest honest test of whether an offer can carry attention. After thirty days you will know whether to add the second one or fix the first, and you will know it from evidence instead of hope.
tiktok.cap: One offer, thirty days, then add the second. That is the whole test.
tiktok.body: One offer, same offer, thirty days, different angle. Not because the others are bad but because thirty days is the shortest honest test of whether an offer can carry attention. Then you will know what to add.

instagram.cap:
You do not need a new strategy, you need thirty days of the same offer so that the results mean something. Change the angle, not the offer.

Thirty days is the shortest honest test there is.

facebook.body:
Lead with one offer for thirty days. Same offer, every post, different angle.

Not because the others are bad — because thirty days is the shortest honest test of whether an offer can carry attention.

After that you will know whether to add the second one or fix the first.

Which offer would you choose for thirty days?

posts.topic: A fear of losing the wrong customer
posts.why: Explains the psychology behind a common mistake.

tiktok.hook: Broad offers are a fear of losing the wrong customer.
beats: The right customer cannot see themselves
tiktok.vo: Broad offers are a fear of losing the wrong customer, and the result is you lose the right one. When you try to be for everybody, nobody can see themselves in the sentence, and the person with a specific problem and money to solve it is the first to leave, because they need to be understood more than they need a bargain.
tiktok.cap: Trying to keep everyone loses the person who would have paid.
tiktok.body: Broad offers are a fear of losing the wrong customer. When nobody can see themselves in your sentence, the person with a real problem and money to solve it leaves first — because they need to be understood more than they need a bargain.

instagram.cap:
The customer you were afraid to lose was never going to buy. The one who would have bought needed to hear their specific problem named out loud.

Being understood is worth more than being available.

facebook.body:
Broad offers are usually a fear of losing the wrong customer. The result is that you lose the right one.

When nobody can see themselves in your sentence, the person with a specific problem and money to solve it leaves first — because they need to feel understood more than they need a bargain.

Who are you actually for?

posts.topic: The caterer who stopped doing events
posts.why: Narrowing looking like shrinking is a fear worth naming.

tiktok.hook: A caterer stopped doing events and got more weddings.
tiktok.vo: A caterer removed everything except weddings from her page. Enquiries went down by about a third, and bookings went up, because the people who arrived were planning a wedding and she was obviously the wedding person. Narrowing looked like shrinking for six weeks, and then it looked like the only decision that mattered.
tiktok.cap: Fewer enquiries, more bookings. Narrowing looked like shrinking first.
tiktok.body: She took everything except weddings off her page. Enquiries fell by about a third. Bookings went up, because the people who arrived were planning weddings and she was obviously the wedding person. Narrowing looks like shrinking for about six weeks.

instagram.cap:
Fewer people asked her about events. More people asked her about weddings. The enquiries she lost were never going to become bookings, which is the part that took six weeks to believe.

The wrong enquiries are not a pipeline. They are a queue of people who will not buy.

facebook.body:
A caterer took everything except weddings off her page.

Enquiries went down by about a third. Bookings went up — because everyone who arrived was planning a wedding, and she was obviously the wedding person.

Narrowing looked like shrinking for six weeks, then it looked like the only decision that mattered.

What could you take off your page?

posts.why: A written exercise with a physical action attached.

tiktok.hook: Write down everything you sell, then circle what actually pays.
tiktok.vo: Write down everything you sell on the left, and everything that actually pays on the right. The right column will be shorter, and it will not match the order on your website. Circle one thing in the right column and lead with it for thirty days. That is the whole exercise, and most people have never done it because the left list is more fun.
tiktok.cap: Two lists: what you sell, and what pays. Circle one from the second.
tiktok.body: Write everything you sell, then everything that pays. The second list will be shorter and will not match your website's order. Circle one and lead with it for a month.

instagram.cap:
Most businesses have never written the second list, because the first one is more fun and makes the business feel bigger than it is.

The list that pays is shorter and less interesting. Start there.

facebook.body:
Write two lists tonight.

Left: everything you sell.
Right: everything that actually pays.

The right column will be shorter, and it will not match the order on your website.

Circle one thing in the right column and lead with it for thirty days.

Most people have never done this, because the left list is more fun.

posts.topic: Your cheapest offer is the loudest
posts.why: A profitability insight disguised as a design note.

tiktok.hook: Your cheapest offer is the loudest thing on your page.
tiktok.vo: Your cheapest offer is the loudest thing on the page, because cheap things travel and expensive things sit still. That is fine if the cheap thing leads to the expensive one, and it is fatal if it does not, because you have rented your best real estate to the thing that cannot pay the rent.
tiktok.cap: Cheap things travel. Expensive things pay. Choose which one gets the top of the page.
tiktok.body: The cheapest thing you sell will always get the most attention, because cheap things travel. That is fine if it leads somewhere, and fatal if it does not — you have rented your best space to the thing that cannot pay rent.

instagram.cap:
If the loudest thing on your page is also the least profitable, the page is arranged by accident rather than by intention. Reordering costs nothing.

Attention and revenue are not the same axis.

facebook.body:
Your cheapest offer is almost certainly the loudest thing on your page, because cheap things travel and expensive things sit still.

That is fine if the cheap thing leads to the expensive one. It is fatal if it does not, because you rented your best space to the thing that cannot pay the rent.

What is at the top of yours?

posts.why: The failure is total, which makes it memorable.

tiktok.hook: I read people nine services. Nobody could repeat one back.
beats: It was catering, because she likes food
tiktok.vo: I read people a list of nine services and asked them to repeat one back. Not one person could, apart from one woman who remembered catering because she likes food. Nine services read aloud is noise. One service read aloud is a business, and you have about four seconds to be the second thing.
tiktok.cap: Nine services read aloud is noise. One is a business.
tiktok.body: Nine services, thirty seconds, one recollection — and that was because she likes food. Everything you add to the list makes the whole thing harder to hold in a head.

instagram.cap:
Word of mouth requires a sentence short enough to pass on. Nine services is not a sentence, it is a brochure, and nobody repeats a brochure.

If it cannot be repeated, it will not be referred.

facebook.body:
I read people a list of nine services and asked them to repeat one back.

Not one person could — apart from one woman who remembered catering because she likes food.

Nine services read aloud is noise. One service read aloud is a business.

And you have about four seconds to be remembered.

What would you want repeated?

posts.topic: The landing page kit is for one offer
posts.why: The product's constraint is also the diagnosis.

tiktok.vo: The landing page kit builds one page for one offer with one action. It is useless if you refuse to choose, which is why the people who need it most are the ones with nine services. Five thousand naira. Pick the offer that pays, and the kit does the rest of the deciding for you.

Most page builders let you add a tenth service. This one is built around the assumption that you should not.

A tool that forces a decision is worth more than one that avoids it.

posts.why: Refusing the bigger job is the most persuasive sales story there is.

tiktok.hook: We turned down a rebrand. The business needed a sentence.
beats: Cheaper for them, less for us
tiktok.vo: Someone asked us to rebrand a nine service business: logo, colours, photos, the whole six weeks. We said no, because the brand was fine and the offer was the problem. We sold them a one page offer document instead, which cost a fifth as much and took four days. They were annoyed for a week and then the enquiries changed. That is the only kind of sales story I trust.
tiktok.cap: They asked for six weeks of rebranding. They needed a sentence. We sold the sentence.
tiktok.body: Logo, colours, photos — six weeks of brand work for a business whose brand was fine and whose offer was the problem. We sold a one-page offer document instead. Cheaper for them, less for us, and the enquiries changed.

instagram.cap:
A new logo would have made the same nine services look tidier. It would not have made anyone choose one, which was the entire problem.

The most useful sale is sometimes the smallest one.

facebook.body:
Someone asked us to rebrand a nine-service business: logo, colours, photos, the full six weeks.

We said no. The brand was fine. The offer was the problem.

We sold them a one-page offer document instead, which cost a fifth as much and took four days.

They were annoyed for a week. Then the enquiries changed.

When did a smaller job do more?

posts.topic: Write your one offer in a sentence
posts.why: Three fields, one breath. The day's takeaway.

tiktok.hook: Write your one offer in a sentence: who, what, by when.
tiktok.vo: Write your one offer in a sentence with three parts: who it is for, what they get, and by when. Small restaurants in Yaba, a one page site that works on a phone, in seven days. Who, what, by when. If you cannot fill in the by when, you do not have an offer, you have an interest.
tiktok.cap: Who · What · By when. One breath. If you cannot date it, it is not an offer.
tiktok.body: Who it is for, what they get, by when. If you cannot fill in the by-when, you do not have an offer yet — you have an interest, and interests do not sell.

instagram.cap:
A date is the part everyone leaves out, and it is the part that turns a description into something a customer can say yes to.

No date means no offer, only an interest.

facebook.body:
Write your one offer in a sentence with three parts: who it is for, what they get, and by when.

Example: small restaurants in Yaba, a one-page site that works on a phone, in seven days.

Who. What. By when.

If you cannot fill in the 'by when', you do not have an offer. You have an interest.

Write yours in the comments.
